extracted.intended_audience: researchers and teams planning or conducting scoping reviews (including trainees, librarians, and knowledge synthesis teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and best-practice criteria for planning, conducting, and reporting scoping reviews—covering question formulation, protocol development, search and selection methods, data charting, synthesis, and reporting. Geared to research teams producing scoping reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "A scoping review or scoping study is a form of knowledge synthesis that addresses an exploratory research question aimed at mapping key concepts, types of evidence, and gaps in research related to a defined area or field by systematically searching, selecting, and synthesizing existing knowledge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to set expectations: the goal is mapping concepts, evidence types, and gaps in a defined field via systematic search, selection, and synthesis rather than focused effect estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate purposes for a scoping review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons to do a scoping review include: determine the ability to conduct a systematic review; summarize and disseminate research findings; identify research gaps; make recommendations for future research; map a body of literature with relevance to time, location, source, and origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly justify that a scoping review fits your aims (e.g., exploratory mapping, gap identification). Avoid framing rationale negatively (e.g., 'because we are not assessing quality').

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding to do a scoping review (prior work and users)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting: check whether a scoping review has already been done; perform protocol and scoping-review searches (e.g., PROSPERO); understand who the knowledge users are for the review; consider how a consultation phase might fit the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document searches for existing reviews and identify key stakeholders/knowledge users early; incorporate their input into framing and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol and written plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider publishing a protocol or at least develop a written plan of action that details criteria for inclusion/exclusion, what data are relevant, and how data will be extracted and mapped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get feedback from knowledge users; use PRISMA-P for protocol structure. A protocol should reflect the iterative nature of scoping reviews while pre-specifying methods to enhance transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title clarity: include 'Scoping review' and use PCC
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 'Scoping review' in the title. Use the PCC mnemonic: Population (Who), Concept (What), Context (With what qualifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear labeling (title) and PCC framing help readers immediately understand scope and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear review question(s), objectives, and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: State the review question, objective, and purpose. Explain why the body of literature needs summarizing and for whom; specify what you want to accomplish and how results will advance knowledge or practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid missing the purpose. Align methods and outputs to the stated objectives and intended knowledge users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search methods: reproducible, comprehensive documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe searches such that they could be repeated by others. Describe all information sources (databases with dates of coverage), whether authors were contacted, date last searched, and any limits (publication status, time, language). Include grey literature, reference list searching, and hand searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full search details (databases, coverage dates, search dates, limits, and search strategies) to allow reproducibility and demonstrate comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion/exclusion criteria are vital for decision making and should be explicit (not vague statements like 'we included studies that were consistent with the research question'). Exclusion criteria are equally important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine and document criteria in the protocol; ensure they map to the PCC/question and guide screening and extraction consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening procedures: dual review and consistent application
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 2 reviewers for all screening. Apply the same criteria at level 1 (title/abstract) and level 2 (full text), noting that level 2 uses the full text article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent dual screening with procedures for resolving disagreements to reduce selection bias and increase reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction/charting: defined variables and pilot testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use two people for extraction; list and define all variables for which data were sought and develop a data extraction (charting) guide. Avoid vague approaches like 'we extracted anything in the paper related to the construct of interest.' Pilot test the extraction form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine charted variables, operational definitions, and processes; pilot and refine extraction to improve consistency and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis plan specified and analytical interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly outline the synthesis plan in the methods. Ensure the synthesis is more than just a superficial summary of all the studies; include analytical interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how charted data will be collated, summarized, and presented (e.g., thematic mapping, descriptive summary) and plan for higher-level interpretation relating to objectives and gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation aligned with objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results in diagrammatic or tabular form (numerical summary), and/or in a descriptive format (narrative summary) that aligns with the study objectives and scope. Ensure outputs are consistent with the stated purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual mappings and tables to reflect the mapping goals; include a PRISMA flow diagram to document study selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PRISMA flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a PRISMA flow diagram to document the flow of information through the different phases of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PRISMA guidance for reporting selection numbers at each stage to enhance transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting transparency of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Report (transparently) all details of the methods undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough methods reporting allows readers to evaluate decisions and reproducibility; transparency is emphasized throughout the conduct and write-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope decisions must align with the question
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider carefully decisions that reduce the scope (depth and breadth) of the review. Resource and time constraints alone are not adequate reasons to reduce scope. Limits must be consistent with the question asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restrictions are applied, justify them relative to the review question and intended outputs; avoid arbitrary narrowing that undermines the mapping purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid weak rationales (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor reason to do a scoping review: doing it primarily to confirm there is no literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the review has a substantive, constructive purpose (e.g., mapping, informing future research), not merely a check for absence of literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling interventions in scoping reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing interventions in a scoping review can be done either with or without a review of effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide and state whether intervention effects will be summarized; align methods (e.g., charting, possible critical appraisal) with that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team/skills considerations and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand who the knowledge users are and get feedback from them; 'knowledge syntheses are team sports'—consider team composition and trainee involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders and ensure appropriate team skills (e.g., content experts, methodologists, information specialists) to improve relevance, methodological rigor, and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and follow existing methodological guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult and use established methodological guidance for scoping reviews (e.g., Arksey & O'Malley 2005; Levac et al. 2010; Colquhoun et al. 2014; Peters et al. 2015; Joanna Briggs Guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage these resources (including Joanna Briggs supplements) to inform protocol, methods, and reporting choices; watch for reporting standards such as PRISMA-ScR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document search metadata (date last searched and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report date last searched and any limits (publication status, time, language) on the types of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these metadata in methods so readers understand the currency and restrictions of the evidence base.
